notes: Candidate pool, unlabelled and unfiltered: input to human selection, not an evaluation set. Composition follows evals/METHODOLOGY.md, scaled from the 120 questions decided there to 140 and widened from five categories to the eight the schema defines. The methodology's five-way split (fact 35% / comparison 20% / multihop 12% / adversarial 18% / unanswerable 15%) is preserved in relative terms over the 121 questions in those five categories (fact 34.7% / comparison 19.8% / multihop 11.6% / adversarial 19.8% / unanswerable 14.0%); the remaining 19 slots go to the three categories the methodology did not name -- ambiguous (6), version_sensitive (7) and noisy (6) -- each above the five-question floor the validator enforces for a breakdown row. Adversarial items draw on the T1-T13 trap list in METHODOLOGY.md section 8. Because that section established that Uniswap/PancakeSwap duplication is conceptual rather than lexical (zero PancakeSwap chunks above 0.7 TF-IDF cosine to any Uniswap chunk), the fork traps here turn on shared concepts and diverging values -- fee tiers, Permit2 spender, router revert semantics -- not on copied wording. The corpus's genuine lexical duplication is intra-Binance (mainnet/testnet/Demo Mode), and it is used for both adversarial and version_sensitive items. Every answerable question was grepped against chunks.jsonl before it was written; every unanswerable one was confirmed to have zero supporting hits. source_chunk_ids are provenance only and are NOT gold labels: they record where a question came from and let the annotator notice when the candidate pool fails to surface it. gold_chunk_ids and reference_answer are empty by design at this version.
